purpose: Reconcile the three Foundations certification simulators with the applied scenario style and published item mechanics without using live, recalled, screenshot-derived, or dump content.

CCAO-F.simulatorMultipleResponsePolicy: one original select-two concept per domain per form; this is a practice design choice, not a claimed official item-type percentage

CCDV-F.simulatorMultipleResponsePolicy: one original select-two concept per domain per form; this is a practice design choice, not a claimed official item-type percentage

CCAR-F.publishedScenarioSelection: 4 scenarios drawn from a bank of 6
CCAR-F.simulatorStructure: four 15-item scenario blocks selected from the six published contexts, while retaining blueprint domain geometry
CCAR-F.simulatorMultipleResponsePolicy: one original select-two concept per domain per form; this is a practice design choice, not a claimed official item-type percentage

allowed: official exam guides and public program pages
high-level practitioner reports about style and difficulty
independently authored practice material used only for structural calibration
blocked: screenshots or transcriptions of protected exam items

implementation.practiceAndAdaptive: Existing family/objective coverage is retained. Runtime scenario enrichment replaces generic lead-ins with richer role, evidence, operational, and accountability constraints while preserving the tested concept and answer key.
implementation.fullMock: A dedicated Foundations scenario layer builds the official item count and existing blueprint domain allocation. Select-multiple items are project-original and simulation-only, so they do not alter the validated two-deep concept banks.
implementation.CCARF: Scenario blocks use the published six contexts and choose four per form. Questions are assigned to the selected contexts at form construction while the domain allocation remains 16/11/12/12/9.
implementation.scoring: Select-multiple items use all-or-nothing item scoring. Raw simulator accuracy is never presented as a conversion to the published scaled score.
